newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-NEWCASTLE FLOAT COULD RAISE 50 MLN POUNDS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NEWCASTLE FLOAT COULD RAISE 50 MLN POUNDS.

text.p: English premier league soccer club Newcastle United said on Thursday it planned to raise between 40 and 50 million pounds ($67-84 million) through its stock market flotation this spring.
The club said that it planned to appoint a new non-executive chairman for the holding company before flotation but that Sir John Hall would remain as chairman of the soccer club.
A statement issued through bankers NatWest Markets said the proceeds of the flotation would be used to recapitalise the company and provide a strong basis for future growth.

"Sir John Hall will remain as chairman of NUFC, maintaining his commitment to the football club and focusing his energies and drive on the development of a centre of excellence aimed at encouraging young footballers in conjunction with the new team manager Kenny Dalglish," the statement said.
At least 10 percent of the new shares to be issued will be available to the public via a retail offer with a minimum level of application of 500 pounds.

The statement added that Newcastle United's interests in rugby union, ice hockey and basketball had been sold in July 1996 to The Sporting Club Limited, a company controlled by a number of Newcastle United directors.
